// Component to handle route synchronization with i18n
const RouteSynchronizer = () => {
  const location = useLocation();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const { i18n } = useTranslation();

  useEffect(() => {
    // Force re-navigation when i18n changes and URL doesn't match current route
    const handleLanguageChange = () => {
      const currentPath = window.location.pathname;
      if (location.pathname !== currentPath) {
        navigate(currentPath, { replace: true });
      }
    };

    i18n.on('languageChanged', handleLanguageChange);
    return () => {
      i18n.off('languageChanged', handleLanguageChange);
    };
  }, [location, navigate, i18n]);

  return null;
};

Before downgrading let's try this analysis I got externally. Since I'm weary about downgrading becuase I tried that earlier and it broke a bunch of functionality. I want to avoid downgrading unless we're 100% certain that is the actual case/fix.

Revert all the current changes so we can start fresh and look into this analysis:

That combination is extremely picky about how the router instance is created and shared.
Root cause (spotted in your code)
App.tsx line 2-3:

import { createBrowserRouter, RouterProvider } from 'react-router-dom';
import { router } from './router';

and router.ts starts with:

export const router = createBrowserRouter([...]);

Because router is defined at the top level of a module, every time Vite’s HMR replaces that module (which happens any time you edit any file imported by router.ts), a new router object is created.
RouterProvider receives a different object identity, so React Router thinks nothing changed and does not re-render even though the URL changed.
Fix (keep a stable router instance)
Move the router creation inside the React lifecycle so it is created only once:
Rename router.ts → router.tsx (or keep the name if you like).
Replace the export with a function that returns the router:

// router.tsx
import { createBrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import RootLayout from './layouts/RootLayout';
import HomePage from './pages/HomePage';
// …other imports…

export function createAppRouter() {
  return createBrowserRouter([
    {
      path: '/',
      element: <RootLayout />,
      children: [
        { index: true, element: <HomePage /> },
        { path: 'callsheet/:id', element: <CallsheetPage /> },
        // …
      ],
    },
  ]);
}

In main.tsx (or index.tsx) create the router once and never recreate it:

import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import { RouterProvider } from 'react-router-dom';
import { createAppRouter } from './router';
import './index.css';

const router = createAppRouter();   // only executed once

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <RouterProvider router={router} />
  </React.StrictMode>
);

Delete any router export that is not wrapped in a function.
